title: Data and specified maps of integral support normalization
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a finite-field datum $D$ and closed and open immersions $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$, $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ with $X$ separated finite type over $D.k$. Use the completed coefficient rings, derived complete constructible categories, ordinary module operations and strict quotient-system operations of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], [def-sf-proetale-ring-sheaf-operations], [lem-sf-integral-immersion-pullback-normalization], [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], [def-weil-derived-direct-image], [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], [def-weil-system-operation-exchange-realization], [def-sf-ordinary-integral-comparison-data], [def-zl-ordinary-open-support-normalization], [def-zl-ordinary-open-integral-operations]. Define $\mathrm{closedReduction}$ by ordinary pull comparison followed by the actual strict reduction counit. Define $\mathrm{closedLimit}$ as its adjunction conjugate whenever this map is invertible; define $\mathrm{closedAlpha}$ by ordinary image of the actual reconstruction unit followed by this conjugate. Use the total-limit, reduction and direct-image shift structures induced by the specified adjunctions, and the inverse of the actual direct-image evaluation mate. The structure $\mathrm{Normalization}$ records the inherited geometry and residue-field inverses, these ordinary/strict open and closed isomorphisms with their exact projection formulas, preservation of completeness, constructibility and reduction intervals, the two restricted adjunctions with their four ordinary unit/counit equations and two whole-system open equations, agreement with the specified shifts, exactness, scalar linearity, and the vanishing of the open pullback of closed direct image. This is precisely the existing structure and constructions, without asserting their existence.
